paragraphs: Rav Mari son of Rav Huna, son of Rav Yirmeya bar Abba.
[Berakhot 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.26a.15) has him reporting in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. Hyman says the Yuchasin inferred from this that he was Yochanan’s student.

In [Eruvin 64a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.64a.10) [44a in the supplied Hebrew], Mari bar Rav Huna says that one should take leave of a friend only in the course of a halakhic discussion. [Berakhot 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.31a.13) reads “Mari, son of the son of ר״ה [Rav Huna], son of רי״בא [Yirmeyah bar Abba].” Hyman calls this an error and says it SHOULD READ “son of ר״ה.” He reports that the Gra likewise deleted the extra word. Hyman places Mari in Baranesh, citing [Eruvin 21a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.21a.11-12). Rav Chisda asks him, “You came from Baranesh to Daniel’s synagogue. Why did you rely on the huts? Did not the father of his father [אבוה דאבוה] say in Rav’s name…” etc. Hyman says דאבוה SHOULD READ דאבוך, which gives “the father of your father.”[^4]

notes.text: The Berakhot reading includes an extra generation: “son of the son of Rav Huna.” Hyman deletes the extra word and also proposes “your father” instead of “his father’s father.” Both readings and proposed corrections remain visible. Burganin are huts, not generic supports.

The whole saved Davidson Berakhot 31a scalar 12 really has Mari SON OF THE SON of Rav Huna, son of Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Abba. This corroborates the disputed extra-generation wording, not Hyman’s claim of error or his reported Gra deletion. Hyman’s heading explicitly has full Rav Yirmeyah; the named digital scalar has full Rabbi Yirmeyah, a title difference retained rather than harmonized. Hyman says the wording SHOULD READ son of ר״ה, contextually Huna. In the Eruvin quotation he replaces דאבוה with דאבוך AFTER אבוה: the resulting אבוה דאבוך means YOUR FATHER’S FATHER, not merely YOUR FATHER. The earlier bracketed English which removed a generation is withdrawn additively; the supplied and proposed Aramaic strings remain. The Gra action and Yuchasin pupil inference are source reports, not fresh correction-history or genealogy proof. Uninspected Yochanan remains R-prime; burganin are huts.

Hyman’s print (III, p. 906) gives Eruvin 64a, where the leave-taking teaching is actually found. The supplied Hebrew gives 44a. The consulted Berakhot 26a calls Yirmeyah Rabbi and names Rabbi Yochanan as the source. Berakhot 31a has “son of the son of Rav Huna,” the reading that Hyman disputes. Eruvin 21a has Rav Yirmeyah and reads “the father of his father.” The proposed change to דאבוך after אבוה gives “the father of your father.” Mari answers Chisda’s question by showing him the town ruins, distinct from the huts in Chisda’s question. The claimed Gra deletion and Yuchasin’s pupil inference are reported by Hyman.

[Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2392&lang=en) uses the longer ancestry in Berakhot 31a to propose that Eruvin 64a should add a generation. Hyman proposes removing that generation from Berakhot. The other Eruvin passage distinguishes Chisda’s question about huts from Mari’s reply pointing to town ruins.
